answer: An ocean survey offers a bounty for locating a relic along a spiral route. Entry uses proof-of-work tickets bound to the agent's key, task ID and an unpredictable round seed. Draw the job winner uniformly from valid tickets, not account names, and mark tickets spent. Splitting fixed computing power across a thousand aliases yields the same expected number of tickets as one key, so aliases alone buy no extra influence. Task and round binding prevent reuse. This charges for participation, while leaving hardware concentration and energy costs as tradeoffs.
